topic: The DGX Spark Handbook: real price, day-one path, and the second-Spark rule
title: The $7,999 Spark Handbook Verdict
description: NVIDIA's site now asks $7,999 for a DGX Spark that launched at $3,999. A free community handbook pins down the real price, the day-one setup path, and why a second box buys capacity rather than speed.
hook_candidates: Seven thousand nine hundred ninety-nine dollars. That is the Spark's new asking price.
You've got a Spark on your desk. The second one just doubled in price.
NVIDIA's site wants eight grand for a desk-side AI box.
Four thousand dollars bought a DGX Spark last year. Try five, used.
This handbook settled every Spark setup question in one link.
Your Spark is a memory box. Its doorway is narrow.
Two Sparks, one cable, no merged machine.
A firmware bug chokes fresh Spark clusters to thirteen gigabits.
LM Studio to first model in about an hour.
The handbook's verdict: stop at two Sparks.
narration_full: Seven thousand nine hundred ninety-nine dollars. The Spark's new asking price. Desk or cart, you felt it. One free handbook pinned down the math. Launch was three thousand nine hundred ninety-nine dollars. It has nearly doubled since. Day one: install LM Studio, follow NVIDIA's guide, download a model. You're chatting in about an hour. The Spark is a memory box. A hundred twenty-eight gigabytes of unified memory, one pool processor and graphics share. Big tank, narrow pipe: two hundred seventy-three gigabytes per second. Long prompts break that picture. A second Spark buys capacity, not speed. Buy the second Spark when a model won't fit one box. Two boxes, one cable, never one machine.
analogy: Water tank behind a narrow pipe: a big 128 GB tank draining through a 273 GB/s pipe. Limit: the picture breaks on long prompts, when compute waits less on the pipe.
notes_for_review: Five numbers spent: $7,999, $3,999, one hour, 128 GB, 273 GB/s, one per sentence. Verdict attributed to the handbook. No firmware-bug number to stay inside budget.
